## 1. Load data

```{r}
ROOT <- "C:/Users/gujia/Downloads/independent-capstone-project/Naive_LLM_analysis"   # project root; every path below is relative to it
setwd(ROOT)
if (isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = ROOT)  # keep ROOT for later chunks

df <- read.csv("data/annotated/annotated_50000sample.csv", check.names = FALSE,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
dim(df)
```

## 2. Split Genre into combinations

Each `;`-separated piece of the Genre cell is one combination, e.g. `"fantasy, paranormal; fiction"` → `"fantasy, paranormal"` and `"fiction"`.

```{r}
genre_list <- lapply(strsplit(df$Genre, ";"), trimws)
genre_list <- lapply(genre_list, function(x) x[x != ""])
combos <- sort(unique(unlist(genre_list)))

# syntactic variable names: "fantasy, paranormal" -> "fantasy_paranormal"
clean_name <- function(x) gsub("_+", "_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", x))
data.frame(combination = combos, variable = clean_name(combos))
```

## 3. One-hot encoding

1 = the book has this combination, 0 = it does not.

```{r}
for (cmb in combos) {
  df[[clean_name(cmb)]] <- as.integer(vapply(genre_list, function(g) cmb %in% g, logical(1)))
}

# rename outcome columns: "Absence of Naive Realism_AI" -> "Absence_of_Naive_Realism_AI"
ai_cols <- grep("_AI$", names(df), value = TRUE)
names(df)[match(ai_cols, names(df))] <- clean_name(ai_cols)

# number of reviews per combination
colSums(df[clean_name(combos)])

write.csv(df, "data/analysis_ready/annotated_50000sample_onehot.csv", row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
```

## 4. Linear models (t-tests on each genre coefficient)

### 4.1 Absence of Naive Realism

```{r}
m1 <- lm(Absence_of_Naive_Realism_AI ~ 1 + children + comics_graphic + fantasy_paranormal +
           fiction + history_historical_fiction_biography + mystery_thriller_crime +
           non_fiction + poetry + romance + young_adult, data = df)
summary(m1)
```

```{r}
m2 <- lm(Theme_AI ~ 1 + children + comics_graphic + fantasy_paranormal +
```

## 5. All coefficients in one table

```{r}
res_m1 <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(m1)))
names(res_m1) <- c("estimate", "std_error", "t_value", "p_value")

res_m1$term <- rownames(res_m1)
res_m1$n <- nobs(m1)
res_m1$outcome <- "Absence_of_Naive_Realism"

res_m1$sig <- as.character(cut(
  res_m1$p_value,
  breaks = c(-Inf, .001, .01, .05, Inf),
  labels = c("***", "**", "*", "")
))

res_m1 <- res_m1[, c("outcome", "term", "estimate", "std_error",
                     "t_value", "p_value", "sig", "n")]

knitr::kable(res_m1, digits = 4)
```

## 6. Graph

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Genre predictors
genre_vars <- c(
  "children",
  "comics_graphic",
  "fantasy_paranormal",
  "fiction",
  "history_historical_fiction_biography",
  "mystery_thriller_crime",
  "non_fiction",
  "poetry",
  "romance",
  "young_adult"
)

# More readable labels
genre_labels <- c(
  "Children",
  "Comics & Graphic",
  "Fantasy & Paranormal",
  "Fiction",
  "History / Biography",
  "Mystery / Thriller / Crime",
  "Non-fiction",
  "Poetry",
  "Romance",
  "Young Adult"
)

# Function to extract coefficients and 95% CI
make_plot_data <- function(model) {

  ct <- as.data.frame(coef(summary(model)))

  ct$term <- rownames(ct)

  names(ct)[1:4] <- c(
    "estimate",
    "std_error",
    "t_value",
    "p_value"
  )

  ct <- ct %>%
    filter(term %in% genre_vars) %>%
    mutate(
      lower = estimate - 1.96 * std_error,
      upper = estimate + 1.96 * std_error,
      significance = case_when(
        p_value < .001 ~ "***",
        p_value < .01 ~ "**",
        p_value < .05 ~ "*",
        TRUE ~ "ns"
      ),
      term = factor(
        term,
        levels = genre_vars,
        labels = genre_labels
      )
    )

  return(ct)
}
```

```{r}
plot_data_m1 <- make_plot_data(m1)

p1 <- ggplot(plot_data_m1,
             aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +

  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(xmin = lower, xmax = upper),
    width = 0.2,
    orientation = "y"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(color = significance),
    size = 3
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "***" = "#B2182B",
      "**" = "#EF8A62",
      "*" = "#67A9CF",
      "ns" = "gray65"
    )
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Absence of Naive Realism",
    x = "Regression Coefficient (β)",
    y = "Genre Combination",
    color = "Significance"
  ) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p1
```
